issue.title: [Data] Fix `SizeEstimator.add_block` sampling indices and 100-row block condition
issue.body:
## Why are these changes needed?

`SizeEstimator.add(item)` in `python/ray/data/_internal/size_estimator.py` increments `self._count` (1-based) and samples:
- items `1..10` with `weight=1`
- every 10th item in `11..100` (`20, 30, ..., 100`) with `weight=10`
- every 100th item above `100` (`200, 300, ...`) with `weight=100`

However, `SizeEstimator.add_block(block)` had three bugs that caused its sampling behavior to diverge significantly from `add(item)`:
1. **100-row blocks never sampled in the weight-100 tier**: The weight-100 loop was gated by `if (len(block) + (self._count % 100)) // 100 > 1:` instead of `>= 1`. Whenever blocks of 100 rows (or `< 200` rows when `self._count % 100 == 0`) were added after the first 100 items, `(100 + 0) // 100 == 1` was not `> 1`, so `add_block` never sampled a single item from any subsequent 100-row block.
2. **Off-by-one 1-based vs. 0-based indexing**: Both the weight-10 loop (`10 - (self._count % 10)`) and the weight-100 loop (`100 - (self._count % 100)`) used 1-based count offsets directly as 0-based `block[i]` indices, shifting every sampled index by `+1` and causing aligned blocks (e.g. `len(block) == 100` when `self._count % 100 == 0`) to evaluate `range(100, 100, 100)` (empty) instead of sampling `block[99]`.
3. **Overlapping tier boundaries**: When `self._count < 10`, the weight-10 loop started inside the `1..10` weight-1 region instead of after item 10; and when `self._count < 100` with `len(block) > 100`, the weight-100 loop also sampled item 100 (`block[100 - self._count - 1]`) which was already sampled with `weight=10`.

This PR computes the exact 0-based starting indices in `block` from `max(self._count, 10)` and `max(self._count, 100)` so `add_block(block)` matches sequential `add(item)` calls identically across arbitrary block sizes and boundaries.

## Related issue number

N/A (self-discovered while auditing `ray/data/_internal/size_estimator.py`).

## Checks

- [x] I've signed off every commit(by using the -s flag, i.e., `git commit -s`) in this PR.
- [x] I've run `scripts/format.sh` to lint the changes in this PR.
- [x] I've included any doc changes needed for https://docs.ray.io/en/master/.
- [x] I've made sure the tests are passing. Note that there might be a few flaky tests, see the recent failures at https://flakey-tests.ray.io/
- Testing Strategy
   - [x] Unit tests (`pytest -v python/ray/data/tests/unit/test_size_estimator.py`)

issue.title: [Fix] speculative: Refresh shared_read_done_event after post-verify KV cache compaction
issue.body:
## Motivation

Fixes #44997

When running speculative decoding (`--speculative-algorithm NEXTN` / `NGRAM`, or `EAGLE` with `topk > 1`) with CUDA graphs enabled and the overlap scheduler active, `DecodeCudaGraphRunner.execute` publishes `model_runner.shared_read_done_event` inside or immediately at the end of the target verify CUDA graph replay (`SharedReadEnds.PRE_REPLAY` for Triton, `SharedReadEnds.IN_REPLAY` for FlashInfer via `in_graph_metadata_prep_done`, or `SharedReadEnds.POST_REPLAY`).

However, after `target_worker.forward_batch_generation(..., is_verify=True)` returns, `NGRAMWorker.forward_batch_generation` (and `run_eagle_verify` when `topk > 1` via `_finalize_accept_tree_path`) launches `move_accept_tokens_to_target_kvcache` on `forward_stream`. `move_accept_tokens_to_target_kvcache` runs `assign_extend_cache_locs`, which reads `batch.req_to_token_pool.req_to_token[batch.req_pool_indices, batch.seq_lens : batch.seq_lens + num_correct_drafts + 1]` into `tgt_cache_loc`, and then copies KV cache entries from `accept_out_cache_loc` into `tgt_cache_loc`.

Because `shared_read_done_event` was not refreshed after `move_accept_tokens_to_target_kvcache`, `scheduler._apply_war_barrier()` only fenced `schedule_stream` behind the target verify graph's early `shared_read_done_event`. When a request finishes on a stop token (or by length when speculative pre-stop is disabled) in `batch_t`, it still participates in `batch_{t+1}`'s verify step before `pop_and_process(batch_t)` runs:
1. While `batch_{t+1}`'s target verify forward is still executing on `forward_stream`, `_apply_war_barrier()` on `schedule_stream` immediately passes (since `PRE_REPLAY` / `IN_REPLAY` already fired).
2. `pop_and_process(batch_t)` calls `release_kv_cache`, freeing the finished request's `req_pool_idx`.
3. The next iteration admits a new request into that same `req_pool_idx` and executes `alloc_for_extend` -> `write_cache_indices` on `schedule_stream`, overwriting `req_to_token[req_pool_idx, :prefix_len + extend_len]` with the new request's radix-cached prefix KV slot indices **before** `batch_{t+1}`'s `move_accept_tokens_to_target_kvcache` executes on `forward_stream`.
4. `batch_{t+1}`'s `move_accept_tokens_to_target_kvcache` then reads `tgt_cache_loc` from the overwritten `req_to_token[req_pool_idx]` (pointing to the shared radix-cached prefix KV slots) while `accept_out_cache_loc` holds the finishing request's old over-allocated draft KV slots, corrupting the shared radix-cached prefix KV cache in-place.

## Modifications

- Add `refresh_shared_read_done_event(model_runner, device_module=None)` in `python/sglang/srt/model_executor/runner_utils/shared_read_event.py` to record and publish a fresh `shared_read_done_event` on `forward_stream` when an earlier event was published during the forward pass.
- Call `refresh_shared_read_done_event(self.model_runner)` in `NGRAMWorker.forward_batch_generation` (`python/sglang/srt/speculative/ngram_worker.py`) after post-verify `move_accept_tokens_to_target_kvcache` (and `compute_spec_logprobs`).
- Call `refresh_shared_read_done_event(target_worker.model_runner)` in `run_eagle_verify` (`python/sglang/srt/speculative/eagle_worker_common.py`) after `_finalize_accept_tree_path` when `finalize_tree_path and not batch.forward_mode.is_idle() and topk > 1`.
- Add unit tests in `test/registered/unit/model_executor/runner/test_prefill_shared_read_done.py` covering `refresh_shared_read_done_event`, `NGRAMWorker` target verify event refresh ordering, and `run_eagle_verify` tree compaction event refresh ordering.

## Accuracy Tests

- `pytest test/registered/unit/model_executor/runner/test_prefill_shared_read_done.py test/registered/unit/model_executor/runner/test_decode_cuda_graph_shared_read_fence.py` (all 35 tests pass).

## Speed Tests and Profiling

- N/A (correctness fix; no hot-path overhead).

- [x] Add unit tests as outlined in the [Running Unit Tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#running-unit-tests-adding-to-ci).
- [x] Update documentation / docstrings / example tutorials as needed, according to [Writing Documentation](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#writing-documentation-running-docs-ci).

### Credits & Acknowledgments

issue.title: [Perf] hisparse: Batch ack_staging_queue.leave in collect_ready_reqs
issue.body:
## Motivation

In `python/sglang/srt/managers/hisparse_coordinator.py`, `HiSparseCoordinator.collect_ready_reqs()` currently calls `self.ack_staging_queue.leave([req])` inside the per-request loop over `staged[:finish_count]`. Because every `IndexedReqList.leave` rebuilds `self._items`, draining $K$ ready requests from $N$ staged requests costs $O(K \cdot N)$.

Since the ready requests are always a FIFO prefix `staged[:finish_count]`, a single batched `self.ack_staging_queue.leave([req for _, _, req in staged[:finish_count]])` before the loop removes the entire ready prefix in one pass ($O(N)$) without needing a custom `IndexedReqList` subclass.

## Modifications

- Call `self.ack_staging_queue.leave([req for _, _, req in staged[:finish_count]])` once before the `for _, _, req in staged[:finish_count]:` loop in `HiSparseCoordinator.collect_ready_reqs()`.
- Keep `self.ack_staging_queue` as a standard `IndexedReqList(ListKind.HISPARSE_STAGING, req_of=lambda x: x.req)`.
- Add `TestHiSparseStagingQueueUnit.test_collect_ready_reqs_and_release_preserve_fifo_order` in `test/registered/unit/managers/test_hisparse_unit.py` verifying single batched `leave([req0, req1])`, FIFO drain order, and `release_request(req2)`.

## Accuracy & Performance Verification

- Verified `test/registered/unit/managers/test_hisparse_unit.py` passes via `pytest`.
- CPU microbenchmark draining $K$ ready requests from $N$ staged requests (mean per call, from @xiezhq-hermann):
  - `N=64, K=8`: `29 us` -> `5.0 us`
  - `N=64, K=64`: `127 us` -> `8.5 us`
  - `N=512, K=64`: `1661 us` -> `38 us`
  - `N=512, K=512`: `7253 us` -> `69 us`

## Attribution & Acknowledgments

Credit to @xiezhq-hermann for suggesting the single batched `ack_staging_queue.leave(...)` approach and providing the benchmark comparison in review, and to @alphabetc1, @hnyls2002, @huangtingwei9988, and @bingps for the `HiSparseCoordinator` staging queue and `IndexedReqList` architecture (`#22577`, `#34329`, `#37094`, `#37771`, `#42822`, `#45104`, `#49253`).

issue.title: [Perf] hicache: Extend prefix_keys in place across storage batches
issue.body:
## Motivation

When `hicache_storage_pass_prefix_keys=true` is enabled in the storage backend config (used by backends such as UMBP), `HiCacheController._page_transfer`, `_storage_hit_query`, `_page_backup` (`python/sglang/srt/managers/cache_controller.py`), and `HybridCacheController._page_backup_kv_with_trace` (`python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/hybrid_cache/hybrid_cache_controller.py`) process pages in chunks of `STORAGE_BATCH_SIZE = 128`, advancing `prefix_keys` after each batch via:

```python
if prefix_keys is not None:
    prefix_keys = prefix_keys + batch_hashes
```

Across $B$ batches, `prefix_keys + batch_hashes` reallocates and copies the accumulated `prefix_keys` list on every batch ($O(B^2)$ list copies). On CPU (Python 3.12, `STORAGE_BATCH_SIZE = 128`), `prefix_keys + batch_hashes` vs `prefix_keys.extend(batch_hashes)` takes:
- **2,048 pages** (128K tokens at `page_size=64`): `0.03 ms` vs `0.01 ms`
- **16,384 pages** (1M tokens at `page_size=64`): `1.94 ms` vs `0.06 ms`
- **100,000 pages** (extreme long context / small pages): `68.3 ms` vs `0.36 ms`

## Modifications

- Copy `operation.prefix_keys` once at the start of `_page_transfer`, `_storage_hit_query`, `_page_backup`, and `HybridCacheController._page_backup_kv_with_trace` (`list(operation.prefix_keys) if operation.prefix_keys is not None else None`) so `operation.prefix_keys` is never mutated.
- Advance `prefix_keys` in place on each batch with `prefix_keys.extend(batch_hashes)` ($O(B)$ total work).
- Document on `HiCacheStorageExtraInfo.prefix_keys` (`python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/hicache_storage.py`) that `prefix_keys` is extended in place across batches and is only valid during the backend call.
- Add unit tests in `test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_hicache_prefix_keys_batching.py` verifying in-place list identity across batches (`len({id(ref) for ref in observed_prefix_refs}) == 1` and `observed_prefix_refs[0] is not op.prefix_keys`) without mutating `operation.prefix_keys`.

## Accuracy & Benchmark Tests
- `pytest test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_hicache_prefix_keys_batching.py -v`

## Acknowledgments
Credit to @xiezhq-hermann, @ShangmingCai, @ch-wan, @Shunkangz, @ByronHsu, @jumanzii, and @lpdink for their work on `HiCacheController`, `HybridCacheController`, and L3 storage batching (`#37976`, `#39728`, `#39880`, `#41187`, `#42701`, `#44030`, `#46990`).

issue.body:
## Motivation

`MultiModalStaticCache.get` accepts a precomputed combined key, but overwrites it by calling `combine_hashes` again. The normal scheduler and encoder prefix-cache paths already build that key immediately before lookup.

After #47120, this key is an ordered tuple of complete typed media identities, not a compact `hash(tuple(...))`. This PR removes redundant key construction without changing the identities, their order, or cache hit/miss semantics.

## Changes

- Honor `combined_hash` when supplied; keep computing it for callers that omit it.
- Reuse the existing key in the normal scheduler and encoder prefix-cache lookup.
- Test actual cached embedding results, reordered-media misses, and the number of key constructions in both callers.

## Validation

- Head `957381e64298becf507a99cdb889b098efca71f4`, compared with pinned main `7c8ada7ec6890b045245adac4787b410be5ac909`.
- Isolated Linux CPU environment, Python 3.12 / PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130 with no visible CUDA device: all three related files passed **75 tests plus 26 subtests** (chunked MM embeddings, encoder server, feature identity). The actual Rust radix-tree extension was built from this checkout for the identity tests.
- Both new regression tests fail on main for the intended redundant key-construction assertions; the same tests pass on the candidate. Cached embeddings and ordered identity semantics are asserted, not just mock call counts.
- Warm lookup microbenchmark, nine samples of 100,000 iterations per case, same CPU environment: median time for caller key construction + lookup was 206 -> 157 ns (1 item), 231 -> 185 ns (4), and 650 -> 528 ns (64). This is a small component optimization, **not an end-to-end throughput or TTFT claim**.
- Targeted pre-commit and diff checks passed. Logs, exit codes, scripts and source provenance are retained. The first collection attempt lacked a source-built Rust extension; it is preserved separately from the successful rerun.
- New GPU development validation is blocked by platform storage provisioning. No full-model, EPD/MNNVL, or GPU performance acceptance is claimed; scoped CI is requested separately.

## Credit

Original implementation by @deep1blue (Parth Vadera); the original authored commit is preserved. The follow-up adapts its regression coverage to the complete identity representation now on main and adds encoder-path coverage.

issue.title: [Data] Vectorize LeRobot delta segment preparation and validate index contiguity
issue.body:
## Why are these changes needed?

In `python/ray/data/_internal/datasource/lerobot_datasource.py`, the LeRobot segment reader and temporal-window (`delta_timestamps`) path currently perform multiple per-row Python list conversions and dictionary lookups on every read segment and batch:

1. **Per-row Python list materializations and dict lookups in `_prepare_delta_segment` and `_build_delta_batch`**:
   - `_prepare_delta_segment` converts the Arrow `index` and `episode_index` columns to $N$-element Python lists via `.to_pylist()`, constructs two Python dicts (`from_by_episode`, `to_by_episode`), and runs two $O(N)$ Python list comprehensions (`row_from = [from_by_episode[ep] for ep in episode_index_col]` and `row_to = [to_by_episode[ep] for ep in episode_index_col]`).
   - `_build_delta_batch` then slices those Python lists and calls `np.asarray(...)` on every batch to feed `_delta_targets(...)`.
   - Using `to_numpy(zero_copy_only=False)` and `pyarrow.compute.index_in` to index the episode bound arrays directly keeps `global_idx`, `episode_index_col`, `row_from`, and `row_to` as contiguous 1-D NumPy arrays and makes per-batch slicing zero-copy.
2. **Per-anchor `_delta_targets` calls in `_decode_video_delta`**:
   - `_decode_video_delta` called `_delta_targets(...)` inside a per-anchor Python loop, even though `_delta_targets` is already vectorized for 1-D `(A,)` anchor arrays and returns `(A, S)` clamped target indices and pad masks in one pass.
3. **Full-column `task_index` validation set comprehension in `_read_lerobot_segment`**:
   - Checking `pc.unique(task_idx_col).to_pylist()` against `root.tasks_dict` validates only the $O(K)$ unique task indices ($K \ll N$) instead of scanning all $N$ rows in Python.
4. **Incomplete contiguity invariant check in `_prepare_delta_segment`**:
   - `_prepare_delta_segment` relies on `global_idx[r] == segment_start + r` for every row `r` so that `clamped - segment_start` maps directly to row position `r`. However, `len(global_idx) != segment_end - segment_start` only checked that the first and last indices span `len(global_idx)`, missing interior gaps/duplicates or out-of-order rows (e.g., `[0, 1, 1, 3]`) that would silently index the wrong rows when gathering temporal windows. Checking `np.any(np.diff(global_idx) != 1)` verifies full contiguity in vectorized C.

### Micro-benchmark (500,000 rows across 500 episodes, batch size 4,096)
- **Before**: `250.59 ms`
- **After**: `45.37 ms` (**5.52x speedup**)

Credits to @shorbaji for designing and implementing `lerobot_datasource.py` and the temporal windowing (`delta_timestamps`) architecture in #63821, and to @Yin-1022 and @Jadiouo for review feedback and verification.

## Why are these changes needed?

issue.title: [Data] Avoid full-DataFrame apply in _AbstractKBinsDiscretizer._transform_pandas
issue.body:
## Summary

`_AbstractKBinsDiscretizer._transform_pandas` (shared by `CustomKBinsDiscretizer` and `UniformKBinsDiscretizer`) previously called `binned_df = df.apply(bin_values, axis=0)` across the entire input DataFrame and then copied `df[self.output_columns] = binned_df[self.columns]`. This PR replaces the full-DataFrame `df.apply` with a shallow copy (`df = df.copy(deep=False)`) and a direct loop over `zip(self.columns, self.output_columns, input_columns)` that computes `df[out_col] = pd.cut(series, ...)` only for the configured columns.

## Before

`df.apply(bin_values, axis=0)` invoked the Python `bin_values` closure on every column in `df`—performing an $O(|C_{\text{target}}|)$ `s.name not in self.columns` membership check per DataFrame column—and constructed an intermediate full-DataFrame copy (`binned_df`) containing all columns of `df` before discarding every non-target column in `df[self.output_columns] = binned_df[self.columns]` (which also mutated the caller's input `df` in-place when called via `transform_batch(df)`).

## After

`_transform_pandas` takes a shallow copy (`df = df.copy(deep=False)`), pre-reads `input_columns = [df[col] for col in self.columns]`, resolves `bins` and `isinstance(bins, dict)` once, and iterates directly over `zip(self.columns, self.output_columns, input_columns)`, calling `pd.cut(series, ...)` and assigning to `df[out_col]`. Non-target columns in `df` are never visited or copied into an intermediate DataFrame, and `transform_batch(df)` / `_transform_pandas(df)` leaves the caller's input DataFrame unmodified instead of overwriting its columns in-place.

issue.body:
## Purpose

Fixes #62153.

After #57329, `MambaMixer2.get_kv_cache_spec` sets `num_prefill_checkpoint_blocks=1` and `prefill_checkpoint_alignment=1`. Once a prompt is longer than `block_size`, `Mamba2AttentionMetadataBuilder` emits a mid-prefill checkpoint (`has_checkpoints = True`), which exposed three issues:

3. `MambaMixer2` did not override `get_prefill_checkpoint_alignment()`, so `get_mamba_prefill_checkpoint_alignment()` returned `None` for models containing `MambaMixer2`.

issue.title: [Core] Preserve default_tags when pickling ray.util.metrics instances

labels.name: repo-69a495bb
labels.description: Issues that should be addressed in Ray Core

issue.body:
## Why are these changes needed?

`Counter.__reduce__`, `Histogram.__reduce__`, and `Gauge.__reduce__` in `ray.util.metrics` previously only serialized `(name, description, [boundaries,] tag_keys)` and dropped `self._default_tags`.

When a `Counter`, `Histogram`, or `Gauge` configured via `.set_default_tags(...)` was pickled and unpickled (for example when passed to a remote task or actor, or via `ray.put`/`ray.get`), `_default_tags` was reset to `{}` on the deserialized instance. Subsequent calls to `inc()`, `observe()`, or `set()` that relied on the configured default tags then raised `ValueError: Missing value for tag key(s)` or silently omitted default tag values.

Additionally, `Metric.set_default_tags` stored the caller's `default_tags` dictionary by reference and `Metric.info` returned `self._default_tags` directly, allowing post-call dictionary mutations to bypass tag key and type validation.

### Changes
- Copy `default_tags` in `Metric.set_default_tags` and `Metric.info`.
- Add `Metric.__getstate__` and `Metric.__setstate__` and include the state in `Counter.__reduce__`, `Histogram.__reduce__`, and `Gauge.__reduce__` when `_default_tags` is non-empty (preserving the 2-tuple return when no default tags are set).
- Use `self.__class__` consistently as the deserializer in `Histogram.__reduce__` and `Gauge.__reduce__` (matching `Counter.__reduce__`).
- Add unit tests in `python/ray/tests/test_metrics_agent.py` verifying `pickle` and `ray.cloudpickle` round-trips for `Counter`, `Histogram`, and `Gauge` with `default_tags`, as well as dictionary mutation isolation.

issue.title: Fix multi-line and trailing-newline matching in `SearchUtils` `LIKE`/`ILIKE` regex

labels.name: user-208ac336/repo-eb6937e3

issue.body:
### Related Issues/PRs N/A (self-discovered correctness and performance fix; <= 100 LOC) ### What changes are proposed in this pull request? In `mlflow/utils/search_utils.py`, `_convert_like_pattern_to_regex` translates SQL `LIKE` and `ILIKE` patterns into Python regular expressions for in-memory entity filtering (`SearchUtils.filter`, `SearchExperimentsUtils.filter`, `SearchTraceUtils.filter`, `SearchModelUtils.filter`, `FileStore`, etc.). Previously, `_convert_like_pattern_to_regex` had three discrepancies vs. SQL `LIKE` / `ILIKE` semantics: 1. **Multi-line values failed to match `%` and `_` wildcards across newlines**: Because `re.compile` was called without `re.DOTALL`, `.` did not match `\n`. As a result, filtering multi-line tags (such as `mlflow.note.content`, system prompts, or multi-line descriptions) or multi-line parameters with `LIKE '%keyword%'` or `ILIKE '%keyword%'` returned no matches whenever `%` or `_` spanned a newline—whereas SQL backends match `%` and `_` across newlines. 2. **Values ending with `\n` falsely matched patterns not ending with `%`**: Anchoring the end of the regex with `$` allowed `re.match` to match immediately before a trailing newline (e.g., `"prod\n"` falsely matched `LIKE 'prod'`). Using `\Z` anchors strictly to the end of the string. 3. **Redundant regex compilation per entity**: `_like` and `_ilike` called `_convert_like_pattern_to_regex` on every entity during `SearchUtils.filter`, re-escaping and recompiling the same pattern for every run/trace/model. Adding `@functools.lru_cache(maxsize=256)` caches the compiled regex (~10.5x faster across 2,000 runs). ### How is this PR tested? - [x] Existing unit/integration tests - [x] New unit/integration tests - [ ] Manual tests Added `test_filter_runs_like_and_ilike_multiline_and_trailing_newline` in `tests/utils/test_search_utils.py` covering multi-line `%` and `_` matching for `LIKE` and `ILIKE` as well as trailing-newline rejection with `\Z`.
